# Before the first class {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

::: {style="margin-top: 1.0em; color:#F7F4ED"}
### Work through this at your desk. Budget 60–90 minutes.
:::

## What you are building

Six pieces, in this order. Each one checks before you move on.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | VS Codium | the editor — Visual Studio Code without the telemetry |
| **2** | Extensions | Python support, from the Open VSX registry |
| **3** | The course materials | this repository, on your Desktop |
| **4** | Python | and a project environment, `.venv` |
| **5** | Ollama + Qwen 2.5 Coder | a language model that runs **on your machine** |
| **6** | aider | the agent you talk to in the terminal |

::: {.warn}
**Session 1 does not include installation time.** Arriving without a working environment means you
cannot take part in either half.
:::

## Where do I type this?

::: {.check}
**Always the VS Codium terminal.** Not the macOS Terminal, not PowerShell.
:::

Open it with **Terminal → New Terminal**, or ``Ctrl + ` ``.

::: {.step}
Why it matters: the VS Codium terminal starts inside your project folder and sees your `.venv`. The
system terminal does neither, which is the single most common reason a command that "should work"
does not.
:::

## Why local, and why these tools

::: {.tight}
- **VS Codium** — the same editor as VS Code, without telemetry, from a registry you can inspect
- **Ollama + Qwen** — the model runs on your laptop. No API key, no subscription, no data leaving
  the machine
- **aider** — an agent in the terminal, so you can see every command it proposes before it runs
:::

::: {.check}
Data sovereignty is a real constraint in the work you will do. A workflow that only functions when
you can send the data to somebody else's server is not a workflow you can take to a client.
:::

## One rule before you start: restart after installing

A terminal reads your PATH **once, when it opens**. VS Codium reads it once,
when it launches. Install something and the window you already have open will
not see it — the command stays "not found" and it looks like the install failed.

::: {.tight}
| After installing | Do this |
|---|---|
| A **VS Codium extension** | *Developer: Reload Window* — `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P` |
| **Python** or **git** | Quit VS Codium entirely and reopen it |
| **Ollama** or **aider** | A new terminal is enough — `+` in the terminal panel |
:::

::: {.warn}
On **Windows** this bites hardest, because the installers change PATH and
nothing already running picks it up — not even a new terminal tab, because the
tab inherits PATH from VS Codium itself. Quit the editor and reopen it.
:::

::: {.muted}
The symptom is always the same sentence: *«… n'est pas reconnu comme nom
d'applet de commande»*, or *"is not recognized as a cmdlet"*. It means the file
exists and your shell cannot see it — never that the install failed.
:::

## Step 1 — VS Codium

Download from **[vscodium.com](https://vscodium.com)** and install it as you would any application.

::: {.step}
You will live in two panels: the **editor** on the right, and the **terminal** below it. Everything
in this course happens in one or the other.
:::

## Step 2 — Extensions

VS Codium uses the **Open VSX** registry, not Microsoft's Marketplace.

::: {.tight}
- **Python** (ms-python) — syntax, linting, the interpreter picker
- **Jupyter** — for running cells inside a file
- **Quarto** — to preview the lecture decks
:::

::: {.tight}
- **Continue** — the assistant panel inside the editor, which Step 5b points at
  your local model
:::

::: {.muted}
Extensions view: **View → Extensions**, or `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + X`.
:::

::: {.check}
**Reload the window afterwards** — `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P` → *Developer: Reload
Window*. An extension that has just been installed is not active until you do.
:::

## Step 3 — The course materials

Download the repository as a ZIP, unzip it **directly on your Desktop**, and keep the folder name:

```text
Desktop/quantitative-methods
```

Then **File → Open Folder** and choose it.

::: {.warn}
Every command in this course assumes you are in that folder. If your paths differ, nothing else on
these slides will work.
:::

::: {.muted}
In Session 02 you will do this properly, with git and your own group branch.
:::

## Step 4 — Install Python 3.12

::: {.warn}
**3.12 specifically.** Not "the latest", not whatever the download page offers
first.
[python.org/downloads/release/python-31214](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31214/)
:::

::: {.tight}
- **Windows** — *Windows installer (64-bit)*, and tick **Add python.exe to PATH**
  on the first screen
- **macOS** — *macOS 64-bit universal2 installer*
- **Linux** — `sudo apt install python3.12 python3.12-venv`
:::

::: {.check}
**Then quit VS Codium and reopen it**, before the next slide. The installer
changes PATH and a window already open will not see it.
:::

## Why 3.12 and not the newest

`aider-chat` declares `requires-python <3.13`. On 3.13 or 3.14 it cannot be
installed at all.

::: {.tight}
- Everything else in the course runs fine on 3.14
- One interpreter is simpler than two
- 3.12 is supported until **October 2028**, well past this course
:::

## Step 4b — Create the environment

From the repository root. **Name the version** — a bare `python3` or `py` picks
the newest you have installed.

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv          # macOS
```

```bash
python3.12 -m venv .venv          # Linux
```

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv            # Windows
```

::: {.muted}
Check first if you like: `python3.12 --version`, or `py -3.12 --version` on
Windows.
:::

## Windows: the star is not a tick

`py --list` marks the **default** — what a bare `py` uses. After installing 3.12
the star normally stays where it was:

```text
 -V:3.14 *        Python 3.14 (64-bit)
 -V:3.12          Python 3.12 (64-bit)
```

::: {.check}
That is expected, and it is why every command writes `-3.12`. Leave the star
alone.
:::

## Step 4c — Activate it

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate         # macOS
```

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate         # Linux
```

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\activate            # Windows
```

::: {.check}
Your prompt should now begin with **`(.venv)`**. If it does not, the activation
did not take, and nothing you install afterwards will be visible to the course.
:::

## Windows: "l'exécution de scripts est désactivée"

Activation is a PowerShell script, and Windows refuses to run scripts by
default:

```text
… ne peut pas être chargé car l'exécution de scripts est désactivée
    sur ce système
… cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system
```

Nothing is broken. Allow scripts **for your own account** — no administrator
rights needed, and it is asked once, ever:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
```

Answer `O` (or `Y`), then activate again.

::: {.muted}
`RemoteSigned` runs scripts you wrote or created locally, and still refuses
unsigned scripts downloaded from the internet. It is the setting Microsoft
recommends for development machines — not `Unrestricted`, and not `Bypass`.
:::

::: {.check}
Would rather change nothing? `.venv\Scripts\activate.bat` does the same job and
is not a PowerShell script — but you must run it from **cmd**, not PowerShell,
and you will need it in every new terminal.
:::

## Step 4d — Install the packages

```bash
python --version                  # must say 3.12.x
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

::: {.warn}
Check the version **before** installing. If it is not 3.12, the environment was
built by the wrong interpreter — see *Built it on the wrong version?*
:::

::: {.muted}
Inside an activated environment, plain `python` and `pip` are the right commands
on all three platforms. The version-naming was only needed to create it.
:::

## Built it on the wrong version? Start over

::: {.warn}
A `.venv` **remembers the interpreter that created it**. Installing 3.12
afterwards changes nothing, and neither does PATH — the folder has to go and be
rebuilt.
:::

**Windows.** Quit VS Codium first — it holds the interpreter it has selected,
and that alone can stop the folder being deleted. Then open **PowerShell** from
the Start menu, not a terminal inside the editor:

```powershell
cd ~\Desktop\quantitative-methods
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .venv
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
```

Now reopen VS Codium, and in its terminal:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
.venv\Scripts\activate
python --version                      # must say 3.12.x
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

::: {.muted}
Still `le répertoire n'est pas vide`? `cmd /c "rmdir /s /q .venv"` deletes it
where `Remove-Item` will not.
:::

## `deactivate` is not a command

It is a function that **activation creates**, so it exists only while an
environment is active.

::: {.check}
*«Le terme `deactivate` n'est pas reconnu»* is not a problem to solve — it is
the answer to "am I in a virtual environment?", and the answer is no. Skip the
step and carry on.
:::

::: {.muted}
The reliable indicator is the prompt: `(.venv)` at the start means active,
nothing means not. On Windows the folder is then held by VS Codium rather than
by your shell, which is why quitting the editor is the step that works.
:::

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
rm -rf .venv
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python --version                      # must say 3.12.x
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

::: {.check}
If `python --version` says anything but 3.12, the `venv` line used the wrong
interpreter — check you wrote `-3.12` — and you need to delete and rebuild
again.
:::

## Windows: still cannot activate?

Work through it in this order:

::: {.step}
**Does `.venv` exist?** `ls .venv\Scripts` should list `activate`,
`activate.bat` and `Activate.ps1`. If not, the `venv` command failed — read its
output rather than moving on.
:::

::: {.step}
**Is it the execution policy?** *«l'exécution de scripts est désactivée»* — see
the slide above. This is the usual answer.
:::

::: {.step}
**Spelling.** `activate`, not `activiate`. Tab-completion after
`.venv\Scripts\a` will finish it for you and never misspells it.
:::

::: {.muted}
Prefer the star on 3.12? `setx PY_PYTHON 3.12`, then a new terminal. Not needed
for anything in this course, which always names the version.
:::

## Windows: "Python introuvable"

If `py` or `python` prints **Python introuvable / Python was not found** and
offers you the Microsoft Store, do **not** accept. There are two causes and the
first is the common one.

::: {.step}
**1 · The Store alias is shadowing Python.** Windows ships a stub named
`python.exe` that does nothing but open the Store.

Start → search **Manage app execution aliases** → turn **off** both
**python.exe** and **python3.exe**. Close the terminal and open a new one.
:::

::: {.step}
**2 · Python is not installed, or not on PATH.** Install from
[python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/) — not the Store — and
on the first screen tick **Add python.exe to PATH** before clicking Install.
That checkbox is off by default and is the single most common setup failure.
:::

## Windows: checking it took

Open a **new** terminal — PATH changes do not reach a terminal that is already
running.

```powershell
py --version
where py
```

::: {.check}
A version number and a path under `Program Files` or `AppData` means you are
fine. A path ending in `WindowsApps` means the Store alias is still in the way:
go back and turn it off.
:::

::: {.muted}
`py` is the right command on Windows even once PATH is set — it finds every
installed version and picks the newest. Inside an activated `.venv`, plain
`python` works and refers to the environment's own interpreter.
:::

## Step 5 — Ollama and Qwen

Install **[ollama.com](https://ollama.com)**, then in the VS Codium terminal:

```bash
ollama --version
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder
ollama pull nomic-embed-text
```

::: {.muted}
The second model is used in Session 09 for text embeddings. Pull it now while you have bandwidth.
:::

Check it answers:

```bash
ollama run qwen2.5-coder "In one sentence, what is a residual?"
```

::: {.muted}
`ollama: command not found` right after installing? Open a **new terminal**. On
Windows, quit VS Codium and reopen it.
:::

::: {.check}
**Turn your wifi off and run that again.** It should still answer. That is the point of running it
locally.
:::

## Step 5b — Open Continue's config file

Installed, Continue still talks to nothing. It needs a config file, and the
easiest way to open it is from inside Continue itself:

::: {.step}
Open the Continue panel → the **gear icon** at its top right → *Configure*. It
opens `config.yaml` in the editor, creating it if it does not exist.
:::

If you would rather do it from the terminal — the file lives in your home
directory, and the path differs:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.continue && open -e ~/.continue/config.yaml        # macOS
```

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.continue && ${EDITOR:-nano} ~/.continue/config.yaml   # Linux
```

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$HOME\.continue" | Out-Null
notepad "$HOME\.continue\config.yaml"                          # Windows
```

::: {.muted}
`$HOME\.continue` on Windows is normally `C:\Users\you\.continue`. The folder
starts with a dot, so File Explorer hides it unless *Hidden items* is ticked in
the View ribbon.
:::

## Step 5c — What to put in it

```yaml
name: qmib
version: 0.0.1
models:
  - name: Local coder
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen2.5-coder:7b     # the size you actually pulled
    roles: [chat, edit, apply]
  - name: Local embedder
    provider: ollama
    model: nomic-embed-text
    roles: [embed]
context:
  - provider: file
  - provider: code
  - provider: diff
  - provider: terminal
```

::: {.check}
Open a `.py` file, select a few lines, press `Cmd/Ctrl + L`. If the panel
answers, you are done.
:::

::: {.muted}
Nothing at all means no model server is listening. Start Ollama — the app on
macOS and Windows, `sudo systemctl start ollama` on Linux.
:::

## Which model size

```bash
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b     # 8 GB RAM
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b     # 16 GB  ← most laptops
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:14b    # 32 GB+
```

::: {.warn}
Pull the one that matches your **RAM**, not the biggest one. A model that does
not fit swaps to disk, and a 30-second answer becomes a five-minute one. Change
the name in `config.yaml` to whichever you pulled.
:::

## Step 6 — Give the model a real context window

Ollama defaults to a **2,048-token** context. aider fills that with your file and
the model then "forgets" what you sent. Raise it to 8192.

::: {.warn}
The setting is read by the **server**, once, when it starts. Setting it in the
terminal where you run `aider` does nothing at all — and you cannot simply start
a second server, because one is already running on every platform.
:::

::: {.tight}
So on all three the shape is the same: **set the variable for the system, then
restart Ollama.**
:::

## Step 6 — macOS

```bash
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH 8192
```

Then quit Ollama from the **menu bar** and reopen it.

## Step 6 — Windows

```powershell
setx OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH 8192
```

Then quit Ollama from the **system tray** — right-click its icon → *Quit* — and
start it again from the Start menu.

::: {.warn}
`setx` writes the variable permanently but does **not** apply it to the terminal
you typed it in. Ollama picks it up when it next starts, which is why the restart
is not optional.
:::

## Step 6 — Linux

Installed by the official script, Ollama runs under systemd:

```bash
sudo systemctl edit ollama.service
```

Add these two lines, save, then reload and restart:

```ini
[Service]
Environment="OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192"
```

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart ollama
```

::: {.muted}
Running it by hand instead of as a service? Then
`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve` is all you need.
:::

## If you see a socket error

```text
Only one usage of each socket address … is normally permitted
Une seule utilisation de chaque adresse de socket est normalement autorisée
Error: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:11434: bind: address already in use
```

::: {.check}
All three say the same thing: **Ollama is already running.** That is the normal
state — the installer starts it for you on every platform. You do not need
`ollama serve` at all; you need the variable set and the running server
restarted, which is what the three slides above do.
:::

::: {.muted}
Check what is answering: `curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version` — on Windows,
`curl.exe`.
:::

## Step 6b — aider needs its own environment

::: {.warn}
**Do not `pip install aider-chat` into `.venv`.** aider pins its own versions of
packages the course also uses, and pip must satisfy both at once — which is where
the resolver errors come from. When it appears to succeed it can quietly
downgrade something the course needs.
:::

::: {.check}
Do this in a terminal where **`(.venv)` is not showing**. `--user` is refused
inside a virtual environment, and that refusal is what leaves you with *no module
named pipx* a moment later.
:::

## Step 6b — Install pipx

**Name the version on both lines.** Installing with one interpreter and calling
with another is the whole of the *no module named pipx* problem.

```bash
python3.12 -m pip install --user pipx      # macOS
python3.12 -m pipx ensurepath
```

```bash
python3.12 -m pip install --user pipx      # Linux
python3.12 -m pipx ensurepath
```

```powershell
py -3.12 -m pip install --user pipx        # Windows
py -3.12 -m pipx ensurepath
```

::: {.warn}
`ensurepath` edits PATH, and nothing already running sees it. **Quit VS Codium
and reopen it** before the next slide.
:::

## Step 6b — Install aider with it

```powershell
py -3.12 -m pipx install aider-chat        # Windows
```

```bash
python3.12 -m pipx install aider-chat      # macOS and Linux
```

::: {.muted}
Written as a module deliberately: `pipx install aider-chat` is the same thing and
works too, but only once PATH has caught up. The module form does not care.
:::

::: {.check}
In a new terminal, `aider --version` should answer. If it does not, the command
is still at `~/.local/bin/aider` — `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\aider.exe` on
Windows — and calling it there works regardless.
:::

## If pipx will not cooperate

pipx is a convenience. A plain environment does the same job with nothing on
PATH to go wrong:

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv $HOME\aider-env
& "$HOME\aider-env\Scripts\pip" install aider-chat
& "$HOME\aider-env\Scripts\aider" --version
```

```bash
python3.12 -m venv ~/aider-env
~/aider-env/bin/pip install aider-chat
~/aider-env/bin/aider --version
```

::: {.check}
That is all pipx does. Run aider by its full path from then on, and it stays
completely separate from the course environment — which was the only point.
:::

## Step 6c — Pointing it at your model

Point it at the server. The variable goes in *aider's* terminal:

```bash
export OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:11434          # macOS / Linux
```

```powershell
$env:OLLAMA_API_BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"        # Windows
```

Then, on both:

```bash
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

::: {.warn}
`ollama_chat/`, not `ollama/` — the second uses the completion endpoint and
gives markedly worse answers. And use the tag you actually pulled: `:3b`, `:7b`
or `:14b`.
:::

## `aider n'est pas reconnu`?

pipx installed it; your shell just cannot see it yet. Confirm it is there, and
where:

```bash
pipx list          # or: py -m pipx list
```

pipx puts the command in `~/.local/bin` — `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` on Windows.
Call it by its full path and it runs whatever PATH says:

```powershell
& "$HOME\.local\bin\aider.exe" --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

```bash
~/.local/bin/aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

::: {.check}
To fix it properly rather than working around it: `py -m pipx ensurepath`
(`python3` elsewhere), then **quit VS Codium entirely and reopen it**. A new
terminal tab is not enough on Windows — the editor itself is holding the old
PATH.
:::

## Step 6d — Ask it something real

::: {.step}
*"Open `qmib.py` and explain what `load` does when the file is already cached."*
:::

Read what it proposes **before** you accept it. aider commits automatically
after each change it applies, and those commits are attributed to you.

```bash
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b --no-auto-commits
```

::: {.muted}
`--no-auto-commits` if you would rather stage the changes yourself. Either way,
you are answerable for every line on your branch.
:::

## Two terminals is the working pattern

::: {.tight}
- **One** running `aider`, where you talk to the model
- **One** running `python`, where you check what it told you
:::

::: {.muted}
Plus the server — but on macOS that is the app in your menu bar, and on Windows
and Linux it is a terminal you start once and leave alone.
:::

::: {.warn}
The checking terminal is not optional. Every deliverable in this course requires
you to document one thing the model got wrong — and you cannot do that without
checking.
:::

## The last check

```bash
python 01-foundations-scenarios-and-tools/00-pre-session/verify_environment.py
```

::: {.check}
Five checks should pass. **Bring the output to class.**
:::

If one fails, the script prints what to do. If you are still stuck, ask Qwen — which is itself a
test of whether your setup works.

## When it goes wrong

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Python introuvable` (Windows) | Store alias shadowing Python | Turn off the app execution aliases — two slides back |
| `ollama: command not found` | Not on PATH yet | New terminal; on Windows restart VS Codium |
| `aider: command not found` | pipx's folder is new on PATH | New terminal; on Windows restart VS Codium. Or `py -m pipx run aider-chat` |
| Resolver errors installing aider | It was installed into `.venv` | Use `pipx`, which keeps it separate — step 6b |
| `pipx` *n'est pas reconnu* | `pip install --user` put the script in a folder Windows does not have on PATH | Run it as a module: `py -3.12 -m pipx …` |
| `No module named pipx` | It was installed for one interpreter and called from another — or `--user` was refused because `.venv` was active | Deactivate, then `py -3.12` on **both** lines |
| An extension does nothing | Installed but not loaded | *Developer: Reload Window* |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` in VS Codium | Wrong interpreter selected | `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P` → *Python: Select Interpreter* → `.venv` |
| `pip` fails | Environment not active | Check your prompt starts with `(.venv)` |
| *l'exécution de scripts est désactivée* (Windows) | PowerShell blocks scripts by default, and activation is one | `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`, then activate again |
| *le répertoire n'est pas vide* deleting `.venv` | Something holds a file inside it — usually VS Codium's selected interpreter | Quit VS Codium, delete from a plain PowerShell. Last resort `cmd /c "rmdir /s /q .venv"` |
| `deactivate` *n'est pas reconnu* | It only exists while an environment is active | Nothing to fix — you are not in one. Skip the step |
| Continue answers nothing | No server on 11434 | Start Ollama: the app on macOS and Windows, `systemctl start ollama` on Linux |
| The model is very slow | Too large for your RAM | Pull `:3b` and change `config.yaml` |
| aider forgets your file | Ollama's 2k default context | Raise it on the server and restart Ollama — step 6 |
| `address already in use` / *une seule utilisation … socket* | Ollama is already running — it always is | You do not need `ollama serve`. Set the variable, restart Ollama |
| `connection refused` from aider | Nothing on 11434 | Start Ollama: the app on macOS and Windows, `systemctl start ollama` on Linux |
| Maths shows as raw `$...$` | No preview extension | Install *Markdown Preview Enhanced*, open with `Cmd/Ctrl + K V` |
| Slow on Apple Silicon | Rosetta build of Python | Install the arm64 build |

## Using the model well

The local model is a **sparring partner**, not an oracle.

::: {.step}
**Ask it to argue against you.** Its most useful output is the objection you had
not considered — not the answer you were hoping for.
:::

::: {.step}
**Verify every factual claim.** It states plausible falsehoods with complete
confidence, and does so most often about library APIs, statistical results and
citations — which is exactly the material of this course.
:::

::: {.step}
**Record what you checked.** Every practice deliverable requires one documented
instance where you caught the model being wrong or unable to support a claim.
That is graded.
:::

::: {.warn}
You are never penalised for using the model. You are penalised for using it
uncritically.
:::
